races.name: Wakefield Thornes Cricket Club Nursery

runners_data.name: Poppy Foxy
runners_data.note: Sets the pace here as the lone confirmed front-runner; secured a win over 7f on Soft last time and drops back to 6f on Good, where her two similar-going runs have not produced a win or place — she may find this trip on a fair surface tests whether her lead is sustainable.|

runners_data.name: Claret And Blues
runners_data.note: Most likely to sit prominently behind the leader and apply pressure through the middle stages; Warren Fentiman (3) takes the ride with Fahey's yard hitting 7/69 in the 14-day window, and three runs on Good or Standard have yet to produce a win but consistency is building.|

runners_data.name: Fasthope
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's 2-year-old is a natural hold-up type who has shown a knack for staying on from off the pace; only one run on similar Going (Good) from three starts, which slightly limits confidence in the ground profile, but the 12-day turnaround for a yard running at 1/21 recently is modest.|

runners_data.name: Priscilla's Hope
runners_data.note: Has one placing in four starts (third at 6f on Good) which represents her best performance on conditions matching today; Philip McBride has only one runner in the 14-day window so no stable form to weigh, and she needs to improve on recent 8th and 6th efforts.|

runners_data.name: Baila Morena
runners_data.note: Harry Russell partners this Ollie Pears runner who is a genuine hold-up horse by nature but has been pushed forward into a midfield mapping here due to the volume of closers in the field — her last three form figures of 7-4-0 on Good ground make her a difficult proposition regardless of where she settles.|

runners_data.name: Black Cuillin
runners_data.note: Joanna Mason takes the mount on this Craig Lidster-trained 2-year-old who has finished fourth in both career starts on Good ground — consistent without threatening — and though she is a natural hold-up horse, the redistribution into midfield means she won't get the run she's bred for.|

runners_data.name: Givendale
runners_data.note: Carries a specific finishing concern flagged in her profile, with form figures of 5-9 in her two most recent runs on Good ground highlighting a tendency to fade rather than finish; Nigel Tinkler has had no winners from 18 runners in 14 days, and the redistribution into a midfield slot compounds her lack of genuine late-run opportunity.|

runners_data.name: Spirit Of Mary
runners_data.note: Lowest-rated runner in the field at OR 45, and Ben Haslam's filly — a true hold-up type — is mapped into midfield due to pace-shape constraints; form of 9-7-4 gives little encouragement, and Andrew Mullen takes over the ride after 41 days off with no market confidence suggested by the yard's modest 14-day record.|

races.paceDynamic: Poppy Foxy is the sole confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner 6f nursery, and with no genuine pace rivals to press her, she should be able to bowl along at a self-regulated gallop from the gates — creating a steady-to-moderate tempo that suits those racing close to the action. Claret And Blues is the most likely horse to track her from a prominent pitch, with the rest of the field — Fasthope, Priscilla's Hope, Baila Morena, Black Cuillin, Givendale and Spirit Of Mary — all natural hold-up types who are unlikely to get their preferred late-run position given how few genuine front-runners are in the race. The field holds more hold-up horses than the pace map can accommodate at the rear, meaning Baila Morena, Black Cuillin, Givendale and Spirit Of Mary will be shuffled into midfield roles that are not truly natural to their style. A steady pace set by an uncontested leader on Good ground at Pontefract's galloping 6f favours horses who race prominently or can sit just off the pace and pounce in the straight, rather than those making up ground from deep.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Poppy Foxy Leads Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Poppy Foxy breaks cleanly and dictates a comfortable pace with no horse willing or able to pressurise her from the off.
scenarios.body: Poppy Foxy sets a regulated tempo throughout, and the prominent racer Claret And Blues — sitting second or third — gets the clearest route to challenge as the field spreads across Pontefract's straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Battle It Out
scenarios.trigger: If Claret And Blues pushes forward aggressively early and forces Poppy Foxy to increase tempo, turning this into a genuine two-horse duel.
scenarios.body: A more pressured pace means the front two tire in the final furlong, and any horse sitting a length or two off — such as Fasthope or Priscilla's Hope — picks up the pieces with a well-timed run.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Storms Home
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is surprisingly strong and the front two burn each other out, allowing a hold-up type to close powerfully late.
scenarios.body: With several horses shuffled into mid-group positions rather than their natural rear spots, a true closer would need everything to fall right — but Fasthope, with some stamina in her form profile, is best placed.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Falls Apart Chaotically
scenarios.trigger: If multiple runners refuse to settle into organised positions, jostling for spots and creating an uneven, stop-start gallop.
scenarios.body: Disrupted rhythm scrambles the usual pace-shape benefits, and the horse with the most tactical versatility — Claret And Blues with her Unknown-style flexibility — may best navigate the chaos.

watchPoints.text: Poppy Foxy's ability to control fractions unchallenged is the hinge of this race — if she gets a clean break and bowls along uncontested, the shape becomes very straightforward; watch whether she is pressed in the first two furlongs.

Claret And Blues with Warren Fentiman aboard may be more aggressive than expected from the gates — if she tries to match Poppy Foxy's early stride, the pace hikes sharply and changes the scenario entirely.

Several hold-up horses (Baila Morena, Black Cuillin, Givendale, Spirit Of Mary) will be competing for a small number of midfield slots; a congested early order behind Poppy Foxy could cause interference or traffic issues in the straight.

Givendale is specifically flagged as a horse that fades in the finish — if she is tracking prominently despite her natural style, she could cause a bumping incident late as she drops back through the field.

The Good going is consistent across all Pontefract races today, so no surface deterioration expected — horses with positive Good-ground form records (Black Cuillin's 2/2, Priscilla's Hope's 2/4) hold a marginal going advantage over those without significant similar-ground experience.

races.name: Noel John Curtin Memorial Maiden Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Hellion
runners_data.note: Four-year-old who has raced at 16f in recent outings, stepping back sharply in trip here; David Nolan takes the ride for Donald McCain but 297 days off the track is a serious concern, and the horse's natural hold-up style means it will not find the compressed sprint finish that this race is likely to produce especially congenial.

runners_data.name: Sixty Plus
runners_data.note: Best form credentials in terms of similar-going record (4W5P from 15 starts), with Joanna Mason partnering for James Owen; drops back to 1m2f from longer trips and the combination of a sprint finish and a jockey strike-rate of only 9/57 over 14 days tempers enthusiasm despite the standout statistical profile.

runners_data.name: Tiernan
runners_data.note: Iain Jardine-trained four-year-old with placed efforts at 11f on Good ground; naturally a closer who finds himself mapped to midfield given the volume of hold-up types, and at OR 85 faces a significant class task against horses rated 35lb higher — the redistribution of his role compounds an already difficult assignment.

runners_data.name: Freddy Fearless
runners_data.note: Lightly raced three-year-old for David & Nicola Barron with just one run to his name, finishing fourth over 8f on Good; running style is unknown and he could easily slot into a lead role by circumstance, making him a key pace factor despite limited evidence — William Pyle takes over in the saddle.

runners_data.name: Kinetic Impact
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand is a strong booking for Charles Hills, and this colt has two starts over 10f on Good ground with a placed effort, giving him the most directly relevant form in the field among the unknowns; his unexposed profile and a top jockey make him one of the most interesting tactical watches.

runners_data.name: Moon Zabeel
runners_data.note: Debutant beaten sixth over 12f on Good for Charlie Johnston; Connor Beasley rides and the horse is a natural hold-up type in a field where that style is congested — having raced once at this exact trip and going, the raw experience base is paper-thin and Johnston's 14-day figures (4/34) do not suggest an imminent peak.

runners_data.name: Steel Raven
runners_data.note: Mikey Sheehy rides for Adrian Paul Keatley, and this three-year-old has run twice — third at 8f and third at 9f — meaning this 10f trip is a step into the unknown in terms of stamina; returned only six days ago, the quick turnaround and Irish-based trainer are worth noting, and style is unconfirmed.

runners_data.name: Khepri
runners_data.note: K R Burke's three-year-old with a single run at 10f on Good, beaten fourth on debut; Clifford Lee takes the ride and the horse is a genuine hold-up type displaced to midfield in this shape — Burke's 14-day numbers (9/53) are reasonable but not compelling, and one run is very little to go on at this level.

runners_data.name: Talitha Rouge
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope is the standout jockey booking in this field, partnering the David O'Meara-trained filly who has placed form at both 12f and 10f on Good ground; her 2W1P in similar-going conditions and a top rider who can read a slowly-run race give her a strong profile for whatever shape emerges.

runners_data.name: Twin And Tonic
runners_data.note: Roger Fell's three-year-old finished last of eleven on debut over 7f on Good ground and now steps up considerably in trip to 1m2f; Oisin McSweeney takes the mount and the horse is tagged as fading in the finish — the combination of a weak debut, trip extension and tendency to fade makes this the most difficult profile to recommend in any scenario.

races.paceDynamic: With no confirmed front-runner in this ten-runner field, the early pace picture is genuinely murky — Freddy Fearless, Kinetic Impact and Steel Raven all carry unknown style tags, meaning any one of them could slot into a lead role by default rather than design, producing a dawdling gallop rather than a true test of stamina over Pontefract's 1m2f. The absence of a dominant pace-setter means this is likely to be a slowly-run affair where the field bunches and the race degenerates into a sprint from two furlongs out — classic Pontefract maiden territory on Good ground. Horses with a sharp tactical turn of foot and the ability to travel smoothly in a compact field will be far more valuable than genuine staying types who need a thorough gallop. This shape strongly favours horses who can travel prominently or mid-division and produce a decisive kick in the final two furlongs; the field holds more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate, with Hellion, Moon Zabeel, Khepri and Tiernan all genuine hold-up horses who are mapped to midfield and are unlikely to fully execute their natural closing role if the pace is as modest as expected.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Slow Burn Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If no runner asserts early and the field drifts into a bunched, falsely-run contest decided in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: The unknown-style runners Kinetic Impact and Freddy Fearless are likely to drift into prominent positions from which they can quicken decisively when the sprint erupts, suiting horses with tactical speed over a trip they've already shown competence at.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Contested Early Pace
scenarios.trigger: If Steel Raven or Freddy Fearless commits to a genuine lead and forces a true-run race at honest fractions.
scenarios.body: A stronger gallop stretches the field and brings stamina into play, which begins to sort out those with genuine staying credentials at 1m2f rather than pure speed; Talitha Rouge and Tiernan, both placed at this sort of trip on Good ground, should be suited by a test of this nature.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Lands Late
scenarios.trigger: If one of the redistributed hold-up types manages to secure a true rearward position and the pace is strong enough to stretch the field.
scenarios.body: Sixty Plus has the best record in similar-going conditions with four wins and five places in 15 comparable starts, and if a genuine gallop develops she has the profile to finish powerfully late; Hellion is the other candidate with a prior placed effort at this sort of trip, though both require a pace scenario that looks less likely to materialise than expected.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Lightly Raced Improver Scores
scenarios.trigger: If one of the unexposed three-year-olds produces a step forward in form beyond what their single run suggests.
scenarios.body: Moon Zabeel and Khepri are both lightly raced Charlie Johnston and K R Burke juveniles from strong stables, and either could hold a substantial unexposed ceiling that renders their debut form misleading; the trainer angles here — Burke at 9/53 and Johnston at 4/34 over 14 days — do not scream immediate readiness, so this remains the least likely shape.

watchPoints.text: Talitha Rouge — Daniel Tudhope's booking for O'Meara carries the most tactical intelligence in the race; watch how she is positioned early as Tudhope is adept at exploiting a slowly-run contest from a prominent berth.

Kinetic Impact — Tom Marquand is likely to position this Charles Hills colt handily given his unknown style, and if he secures a prominent pitch in a bunched field he could prove very hard to pass in the final furlong.

Steel Raven — a six-day turnaround from an Irish handler and an unknown early-pace tendency means this runner could set or disrupt the tempo without warning; if Sheehy elects to make the running, the whole race shape changes.

Sixty Plus — Joanna Mason has ridden this six-year-old twice recently and knows the horse well, but the hold-up style in a slow-run race is a structural disadvantage; only a genuinely strong gallop from the front unlocks her finishing effort.

Tiernan — the OR 85 runner is effectively a 35lb outsider on ratings and faces a class ceiling that form analysis cannot paper over; monitor whether Mulrennan attempts to overcome the redistribution issue by pushing forward early, which would be out of character for the horse.

races.name: Weatherbys Pipalong Stakes (Fillies' & Mares' Listed)

runners_data.name: Bellarchi
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner in sparkling form — five wins from recent starts — and has won five times over seven and eight furlongs on Good; Grant Tuer's filly simply needs a clear lead and her 1-from-13 trainer-14-day record is not a concern given the horse's own momentum.

runners_data.name: American Gal
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's four-year-old has run into double figures repeatedly on Good ground and her OR of 95 looks exposed at Listed level; she naturally wants to race prominently but the crowded pace map means she is very likely to be shuffled back to a position that does not suit her, amplifying an already modest recent record.

runners_data.name: Arisaig
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's five-year-old has an outstanding profile for this race — 14 of her last 15 runs have come on Good ground and she has placed five times at this trip from a prominent position; Jamie Spencer's tactical nous makes her one of the most likely horses to pounce off Bellarchi's controlled fractions.

runners_data.name: Brazilian Rose
runners_data.note: Rebecca Menzies' filly carries a headgear flag and has been running over six and seven furlongs recently, making the step to a mile a slight query; her prominent style should get her into a decent spot but her form on Good ground is thin (just two runs) and she may find the class ceiling here.

runners_data.name: Cheshire Dancer
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's five-year-old has worn a hood previously and has two wins on Good ground from 12 tries at the trip, giving her a recognisable foothold; she races prominently and is the type to benefit from a steady-run race where she can conserve energy for a clean finishing run.

runners_data.name: Consecrated
runners_data.note: William Haggas and Tom Marquand is an attractive combination, and her one win came on Good at ten furlongs; she is a genuine hold-up type but her recent form on soft ground is uninspiring and she needs either a flatter pace or a bunched finish to produce her best late effort.

runners_data.name: Crystal Flyer
runners_data.note: Ben Haslam's five-year-old has a poor recent record — winless and consistently finishing in the rear — and her hold-up style at a mile on Good, where she is 0-from-6, makes it hard to see a route to competitiveness; OR of 85 is modest for Listed grade.

runners_data.name: Goldilocks Cen
runners_data.note: Archie Watson fields a lightly raced four-year-old with only three runs on record and Daniel Tudhope booked to ride is a significant positive; unknown quantity at this level and in this company but her unknown ceiling gives her a sleeper angle if the race unfolds chaotically.

runners_data.name: Mobberley Rose
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's four-year-old has a two-run career record — one win on Standard, one second on Firm — and arrives after 55 days off; she naturally wants to race prominently but with so many front-running types in this field, she faces a real battle to find her natural position, and her inexperience at this level is a risk.

runners_data.name: Mostar Dreams
runners_data.note: Adrian Paul Keatley's five-year-old has won on Good over seven and eight furlongs and holds a genuine hold-up profile, giving her a legitimate tactical reason to be here; Mikey Sheehy must navigate the Pontefract track astutely because any delay in finding daylight will be punished at this level.

runners_data.name: Never Let Go
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's second runner is the more compelling of the pair — two placings from eight-furlong Good races and one win from the trip — and Kieran Shoemark will likely aim to sit just behind the early pace from a prominent position; the 54-day absence is a mild note to watch but her OR of 99 is the highest alongside Bellarchi and Arisaig.

runners_data.name: Radiant Beauty
runners_data.note: James Owen's five-year-old has won twice, including at this trip on Good, and James Doyle's booking elevates her profile; she wants to be prominent but is one of the three runners explicitly displaced by the congested pace map, meaning Doyle will need to adapt and ride her more conservatively than ideal.

races.paceDynamic: Bellarchi is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with only one genuine pace-setter in a 12-runner field, she is likely to control this from the front at a measured, sustainable gallop on Good ground at Pontefract. The redistribution flags on American Gal, Radiant Beauty, and Mobberley Rose are significant — all three are naturally prominent types who cannot all secure their preferred position, meaning at least two will be shuffled back against their will, creating early compression behind Bellarchi rather than genuine pace pressure on the leader. Arisaig, Never Let Go, Brazilian Rose, and Cheshire Dancer complete a crowded prominent group that will jostle for spots in the first half-mile, but without anyone willing to press Bellarchi hard, the tempo is unlikely to be truly searching. This race shape strongly favours the horse who can sit just off Bellarchi's controlled fractions and produce a sustained, quality finish — a well-positioned prominent or closers-with-class profile benefits most, while true hold-up horses face the familiar Pontefract problem of insufficient pace to make ground from the rear on a fair, flat track.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Bellarchi Dictates, Quality Finisher Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Bellarchi is allowed to stride clear and set an even, uncontested gallop and a classier prominent horse sits within a length or two throughout.
scenarios.body: Bellarchi's solo control means fractions will be honest but not brutal, and the first horse to challenge from a stalking position turns the race into a one-on-one; Arisaig and Never Let Go, who have consistently competed at this level from prominent positions, are the profiles who inherit the tactical advantage of a clean run from just off the pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Front Two Clear
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is even slower than expected and Bellarchi's early lead becomes a dominant wire-to-wire advantage before rivals can organise a challenge.
scenarios.body: A pedestrian gallop rewards the horse already in front and any runner tight to her wheel, and Bellarchi's own strong recent form — five wins from recent starts — makes her a genuine danger to last home rather than fade.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Compressed Field, Late Run Lands
scenarios.trigger: If the crowded prominent group creates a wall of horses that checks early momentum and inadvertently lifts the pace mid-race, flattening the race out.
scenarios.body: A more honest tempo through the middle of the race draws the prominent horses' finishing kicks and gives a hold-up type like Consecrated or Mostar Dreams a fraction more daylight to close through a tiring field in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos In Prominent Group Assists Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If the redistribution of American Gal, Radiant Beauty, and Mobberley Rose all trying to push forward creates a scrappy early exchange that disrupts rhythm for the fancied prominent types.
scenarios.body: Disruption in the first two furlongs opens the door to a runner who drops in unaffected and picks up the pieces late; Goldilocks Cen's unexposed profile and Daniel Tudhope's positional awareness give her a narrow route if the race falls apart structurally.

watchPoints.text: Bellarchi has the run of the race — if Oliver Stammers gets her away cleanly and no rival is willing to press her, she may simply be too far clear too soon for a quality hold-up horse to reel in.

American Gal, Radiant Beauty, and Mobberley Rose are all natural prominent types converging on a limited number of early positions — a scrappy first two furlongs caused by their jockeys contesting for those spots could upset the rhythm of several fancied horses.
Never Let Go is having her first run in 54 days for a trainer whose 14-day record reads 3/31 — fitness under pressure from Bellarchi is the key question if this develops into a sustained gallop.

Consecrated and Mostar Dreams are the only two true hold-up horses with any genuine claims — watch whether the pace is sufficient at Pontefract's flat finish to give them a real closing run, as the track does not automatically suit late runners.

Goldilocks Cen has the fewest career runs in the field and Daniel Tudhope's booking for a horse trained by Archie Watson with a live unknown ceiling is worth monitoring in the betting markets for any late market move.

races.name: Pontefract Park Silver Sprint Trophy Handicap

runners_data.name: The Strikin Viking
runners_data.note: Won over 6f on Soft last time, trainer Hamad Al Jehani has modest 14-day numbers and this horse has been off 143 days, but he is a genuine hold-up type whose finishing kick is best served by a faster-than-expected pace — without that injection he is vulnerable to prominent rivals on Good ground.

runners_data.name: Garfield Shadow
runners_data.note: Returned from 593 days off, James Doyle takes over for Hamad Al Jehani, and his two course-and-distance wins show he knows this 6f — his natural front-running style is perfectly accommodated here as the lone pace-setter, though the long absence is the primary uncertainty.

runners_data.name: El Bodon
runners_data.note: Jane Chapple-Hyam's five-year-old is freshest in the field at just eight days since last run and carries headgear; his historical runs label him as a hold-up type yet his form figures at Pontefract are disappointing, and Good ground brings out only 0W0P in similar conditions from 15 attempts.

runners_data.name: Dark Cloud Rising
runners_data.note: David O'Meara and Daniel Tudhope is a powerful combination, and this horse won over 6f on Good at this very trip 19 days ago — a prominent profile that can legitimately challenge Garfield Shadow for the cover position and represents one of the most dangerous threats in this race shape.

runners_data.name: Badri
runners_data.note: Won twice on Good over this exact 6f trip and is in fine nick at OR 92, but his natural prominence means he is squeezed out of his preferred position in a field with multiple horses wanting the front — Jason Hart will need to adapt his tactics, which marginally dilutes his winning chance.

runners_data.name: Beaujolais Nouveau
runners_data.note: Ben Haslam's four-year-old won over 6f on Good but his natural hold-up tendency places him furthest from the pace in a race where the tempo may not be strong enough to bring him into play — his redistribution to midfield reflects a crowded rear, not a style upgrade, and his 25-day absence is neutral.

races.paceDynamic: Garfield Shadow is the lone confirmed front-runner and, returning after 593 days off, faces no meaningful pressure from a rival who will try to dominate — this creates a single-file, controlled tempo from the off on Good ground at Pontefract. Dark Cloud Rising is the only other horse with genuine prominent credentials and is likely to track Garfield Shadow in second, while Badri is a true prominent type who will be squeezed back from his natural position given the traffic ahead of him. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than the map can accommodate cleanly — Garfield Shadow is best-placed to secure the front, with Dark Cloud Rising most likely to take the cover position, leaving Badri and Beaujolais Nouveau to race in roles that do not fully suit them. A single, uncontested pace-setter dictating on Good turf over 6f at Pontefract strongly favours horses that can race handy and sustain their effort through the final climb — prominent racers who travel close to the pace without fighting for it are ideally placed, while genuine hold-up horses face a difficult ask if the tempo is merely steady.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Garfield Shadow Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Garfield Shadow leads uncontested and sets a measured, sustainable gallop that suits closers only if they have significant class in hand.
scenarios.body: Garfield Shadow dictates from the front on a track where front-runners have a strong record at 6f, and with no rival genuinely able or willing to pressurise him, he conserves enough to hold on; Dark Cloud Rising, travelling handy in his wheel, is the chief beneficiary of the honest but unflustered pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Dark Cloud Rising and Badri manage to secure prominent positions and the pace proves honest enough to stretch the hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: Dark Cloud Rising's recent winning form on Good ground at 6f makes him a serious threat if he can settle just off the leader, and Badri's two wins on similar ground show he fires on this surface when racing close to the pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Catch Wall Late
scenarios.trigger: If Garfield Shadow goes too slow early and creates a bunched finish that allows The Strikin Viking to close powerfully from the rear.
scenarios.body: The Strikin Viking has course-compatible form and a hold-up profile that benefits from any late compression, and on Good ground his finishing effort becomes viable if the early tempo is soft enough to leave petrol in the tank.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Goes Too Fast
scenarios.trigger: If an unexpected pace injection from Dark Cloud Rising or Badri forces a faster early tempo that causes Garfield Shadow to tie up.
scenarios.body: A contested early gallop would burn off the front-runners and leave the race to whoever settles best off the pace, though genuine hold-up types here are either compromised by redistribution or carry form doubts that make this a low-probability outcome.

watchPoints.text: Watch Garfield Shadow's behaviour in the stalls and early strides — after 593 days off, any reluctance to stride on from the front immediately hands tactical control to Dark Cloud Rising and reshapes the entire race.

Dark Cloud Rising holds a live each-way position and if Daniel Tudhope pushes him forward to challenge Garfield Shadow for the lead, the resulting contested pace would transform prospects for The Strikin Viking and El Bodon from the rear.

Badri's inability to secure his natural prominent pitch is the key redistribution risk — if Jason Hart sends him forward regardless, he becomes a pace factor rather than a winner candidate and could unsettle Garfield Shadow's rhythm.

The Strikin Viking's 143-day absence and headgear history are worth noting at the off — if he travels with unusual fluency for a hold-up horse in a slowly-run race, Bughenaim may elect to take a closer position than expected.

races.name: Pontefract Squash And Leisure Club Handicap

runners_data.name: Dubai Venture
runners_data.note: Has winning form at 1m2f-1m3f on Good, most recent win coming over 12f on Good ground, and Joanna Mason's record suits; a true hold-up type who will need to find a clear passage late, though the recent 6th over 11f on Soft is forgiven on better ground here.

runners_data.name: Lednikov
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old hold-up horse who has failed to show in five runs at 12f-14f on Good or Standard recently, going 0W2P from 15 similar-going efforts; the 5lb claimer Croot rides but the form profile is against.

runners_data.name: Jedhi Knight
runners_data.note: Has placed form over 16f-17f on Soft but steps back to 14f on Good, where similar-going stats read 0W2P from 14 runs; blinkers fitted and David Nolan is a positive booking, but the unexposed stamina angle on better ground is the key question.

runners_data.name: Clipsham Noble
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner in the race and likely to dictate; recent win over 12f on Good suggests the step to 14f is not guaranteed, and the STYLE_FIT flag at 0.93 reflects that leading here is broadly within role — the pace he sets unchallenged is the defining factor in the race shape.

runners_data.name: Cloudy Rose
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand takes over on this 8yo who has placed form at 14f on Good (5th latest, 5th previously) and is the one horse capable of tracking Clipsham Noble; two career wins at this trip give her a stamina edge, but the trainer's 0/3 in 14 days is a minor negative.

runners_data.name: Yakhabar
runners_data.note: Liam Bailey's yard is in form (2/14 in 14 days) and Yakhabar won over 12f on Standard last time; naturally a hold-up horse running off the back, though the redistribution to midfield means Billy Garritty may find a closer position than usual — blinkers and tongue-tie fitted, and the STYLE_FIT flag at 0.92 tempers expectation.

runners_data.name: Regal Glory
runners_data.note: Roger Fell sends out this 6yo who won over 10f on Good and placed at 14f on Good, showing the trip suits; genuinely a hold-up horse whose best run at this trip came from off the pace, though with multiple closers in the field the redistribution to midfield may actually suit if the run materialises — STYLE_FIT 0.93 noted.

runners_data.name: Princess Vivi
runners_data.note: Headgear (visor) fitted for this 4yo who has a placed run over 12f on Good but has been running at shorter (7f-8f on Standard/Soft) recently; the step back up in trip is a significant query, and her true hold-up style compressed into a midfield slot reduces her chance considerably.

runners_data.name: Apache Eagle
runners_data.note: Ran 4th over 16f on Standard and 4th over 13f on Good in recent outings, showing stamina but no winning form on similar ground (0W0P from 15 runs); tongue-tie and blinkers worn, only 8 days since last run, and the redistribution from rear to midfield means Jason Hart must find cover quickly on a horse that wants to run late.

runners_data.name: Coverbridge
runners_data.note: Has placed once from 15 similar-going efforts and finished 3rd over 12f on Good last time, which represents the form peak; a 4yo whose natural position is at the back, and with the race compressed into midfield for this runner the route to a clear run at Pontefract is congested.

runners_data.name: Muhib
runners_data.note: Consistent placed horse — five runs all returning 3rd or 4th — who stays 12f-14f well on Good and Soft, and the form figures are honest if unspectacular; Warren Fentiman claims 3lb and the horse's consistency over similar trips on similar ground makes him a realistic each-way factor if the pace unfolds cleanly.

races.paceDynamic: Clipsham Noble is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner 1m4f handicap and, with no genuine pace rival to pressure them, Liam Wright can dictate a comfortable, measured gallop from the outset on Good ground at Pontefract. Cloudy Rose is the only other prominent-style runner and is unlikely to challenge Clipsham Noble for the lead, meaning this race will be set at a single, uncontested rhythm with the field strung out behind on Pontefract's undulating track. This field contains significantly more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate — Yakhabar, Regal Glory, Princess Vivi, Apache Eagle, Coverbridge and Muhib are all true hold-up horses redistributed to midfield on the map because they cannot all settle at the genuine rear; in practice, Yakhabar and Regal Glory, with their superior recent form figures, are most likely to secure the closest tracking positions behind the pace. A lone, unhurried front-runner on Good going over a stamina trip strongly favours closers who can travel in behind and pick off the leader in the straight, but with so many horses competing for the same late-running positions, the advantage narrows; the profile that benefits most is a horse that can track prominently in second or third and deliver a sustained challenge rather than one that needs to produce a final-furlong sprint from the back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Clipsham Noble Front-Runs Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Clipsham Noble dictates an uncontested, controlled gallop and the hold-up pack fails to close the gap on Pontefract's stiff finish.
scenarios.body: Clipsham Noble sets a sustainable pace throughout, and with no rival willing to push them early, the lead is never seriously challenged until the straight — by which point the advantage may prove decisive on Good ground.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closers Reel Them In
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely slow and the closers travelling well in midfield produce a sweeping run from the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: A dawdling gallop compresses the field, and the horses best able to quicken on Good going — having been shielded from the early pace — arrive in a late rush to overhaul the weakening leader.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If a horse able to track Clipsham Noble in second or third races more prominently than expected and delivers a sustained challenge down the straight.
scenarios.body: Rather than a sprint finish, the race becomes a test of stamina in the closing stages, favouring a horse with the class to stay within striking range throughout and grind past the leader.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Scramble Develops
scenarios.trigger: If the uncontested pace proves deceptively brisk and multiple hold-up horses surge simultaneously, creating a blanket finish across the field.
scenarios.body: With several redistributed hold-up types failing to find clear daylight at once, the winner emerges from a congested group; form horses with the highest RPR and clearest passage benefit most.

watchPoints.text: Clipsham Noble (Liam Wright) — monitor whether any other runner attempts to race prominently early; if no horse goes to challenge the lead in the first half-mile, the uncontested gallop becomes the single biggest determinant of the race result.

Yakhabar and Regal Glory — both are flagged as redistributed hold-up horses placed in midfield on the map; watch in the early stages whether Garritty or Horgan actually drop them out to their natural rear position, which would leave them with significantly more ground to make up.

Princess Vivi (Cam Hardie) — stepping from 8f back to 14f with a visor fitted for the first time; if she fails to settle in her unnatural midfield position on a track as undulating as Pontefract, she could use up energy she will need later.

Dubai Venture (Joanna Mason) — the form horse on similar going with two wins at comparable trips, but Joanna Mason's trainer is 0/4 in 14 days and the horse needs a clean passage from a hold-up position, so watch the draw and early positioning carefully.

Muhib (Fentiman, 3lb claim) — five consecutive placed efforts suggest reliability but no winning punch; worth monitoring whether the apprentice claim allows connections to secure a prominent enough position to turn consistent placing into a win.

races.name: Go Racing Bet With Jayne Handicap

runners_data.name: Sailthisshipalone
runners_data.note: Won over this course and distance on soft recently with a prominent-to-hold-up blend; the step back to good is a query but tailed-up headgear (tp) shows trainer is trying to sharpen a horse that can drift back in the pack — needs pace to aim at.|

runners_data.name: Flying Fletcher
runners_data.note: Consistent placed form over course and trip on good ground, Ethan Tindall's 5lb claim is a real asset, and a prominent racing style means this horse is ideally placed to travel just behind Welbury and kick when the tempo lifts.|

runners_data.name: Rajapour
runners_data.note: In-form trainer David O'Meara sends a horse who has placed three times at the mile trip in recent outings, but Rajapour's authentic running style is from well off the pace — shown in midfield here only because the hold-up slots are full, which materially dents its prospects in a moderate-paced race.|

runners_data.name: Harswell Ruby
runners_data.note: Roger Fell's mare has placed four times in her last six and carries a headgear flag (p) suggesting she is held together tactically; races prominently which is ideal for this shape, though a tendency to run consistent rather than win is a concern.|

runners_data.name: War Howl
runners_data.note: Worrying recent form string of 990000 with a habit of fading in the finish is a major flag; naturally a hold-up horse shuffled into a midfield slot it does not naturally occupy, and the lack of genuine pace in this race makes a strong late challenge very unlikely.|

runners_data.name: Star Banner
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's lightly-raced three-year-old has placed twice from three starts on good ground at the mile and is unexposed; Rowan Scott keeps it simple from a hold-up position but the small sample and youth mean there is more unknown here than with the older handicappers.|

runners_data.name: Wetsand
runners_data.note: Has not troubled the judge in recent starts with a string of 7-7-5-7-7 suggesting a horse who runs consistently below the threshold; operates from off the pace but James Owen's 10 from 57 in 14 days shows a yard in decent nick which is a mild positive.|

runners_data.name: Welbury
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner in this field and the key pace influence; Daniel Tudhope's tactical intelligence on a horse that has placed three times at the mile on good ground means Welbury is likely to get an uncontested lead, and the STYLE_FIT tag here is about positional mapping rather than unsuitability — this is very much Welbury's race to set up.|

runners_data.name: Mount King
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's older gelding wears tongue-tie and cheekpieces (tp) and has placed three times at the mile on good ground, but is a genuine backmarker assigned to midfield purely because the field is packed with hold-up types — in a pace-controlled race this redistribution significantly limits its winning scope.|

runners_data.name: Clonquest
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced three-year-old who has placed over the mile for David & Nicola Barron and showed ability at listed level on the all-weather; an 88-day break is the biggest concern, and though the stable's 1 from 11 over 14 days is modest, the headgear flag (h) suggests connections are managing a horse that needs settling.|

races.paceDynamic: Welbury is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival for the lead, should stride into an uncontested position from the outset, setting a sustainable gallop around Pontefract's turning mile. The pace will be honest but controlled — Welbury has the rail and the role, and nothing in this field is likely to press hard enough to turn this into a test of stamina. Flying Fletcher and Harswell Ruby will track closely in the prominent positions, giving Welbury company without seriously threatening the lead, which means the tempo stays moderate and the race is likely to be decided in the final two furlongs. This shape strongly favours horses racing prominently or just off the pace who can travel within themselves and quicken when the race ignites — true hold-up horses are disadvantaged by the lack of a searching pace to aim at. The field holds more genuine hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear: Rajapour, War Howl, and Mount King are all natural backmarkers who are shown in midfield purely because the map is full, and Welbury's clean lead means they face an even stiffer task than their redistribution suggests.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Welbury Controls, Prominent Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Welbury secures the lead unchallenged and sets a measured pace that suits those racing just behind.
scenarios.body: Welbury dictates a comfortable gallop with Flying Fletcher and Harswell Ruby in tow, and when the race quickens at the two-furlong pole the horses sitting closest to the pace are best placed to pounce; the lack of a strong early tempo means no advantage accrues to deep closers.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Lifts, Closers Emerge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves stronger than expected and the front rank are left vulnerable in the straight.
scenarios.body: A faster-than-anticipated early tempo drains Welbury's reserves turning for home, opening a gap for those tucked in midfield who have conserved energy; Rajapour and Star Banner, if tracking efficiently rather than buried, would be best placed to capitalise.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Welbury Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow and Welbury's stamina advantage proves decisive against rivals who cannot quicken.
scenarios.body: A pedestrian early gallop paradoxically suits a front-runner who can control the tempo entirely, stealing enough of a cushion that those behind never fully close; Welbury's recent course form and Daniel Tudhope's tactical nous make this outcome plausible if rivals are slow to react.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Swamp Them
scenarios.trigger: If pace collapses early and the field bunches, allowing the deep closers to arrive in a late rush.
scenarios.body: Heavily discounted because Rajapour, War Howl, and Mount King are all racing out of their natural position and depend on a truly contested tempo they are unlikely to receive here; only in an unusually compressed finish would genuine backmarkers have time and space to overhaul a rested front rank.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Flying Fletcher, ridden by a 5lb claimer, can secure a prominent berth directly behind Welbury — if Tindall gets that position cleanly, this horse becomes the most dangerous single threat in the race.

War Howl's recent form (990000) combined with a noted tendency to fade in the finish makes it a horse to oppose confidently; if it drifts in-running, take note as a market signal rather than a form pointer.

Clonquest returns from 88 days off and while the form is not without merit, a first run back for a three-year-old in a competitive handicap deserves caution — monitor in the paddock and at the start for any signs of rustiness.

Rajapour, Mount King, and War Howl are all genuine hold-up horses shown in midfield positions — if the pace is quicker than expected and they find clear runs, they could arrive late, but in a Welbury-controlled moderate gallop this group should be downgraded collectively.

Pontefract's turning mile favours horses who are travelling well rounding the home bend; watch for any horse that appears to be going particularly easily at the two-furlong pole, as the straight is short and positions taken there rarely change dramatically.

races.name: Tallbaldybloke Three Score And Ten Birthday Handicap

runners_data.name: Hover On The Wind
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up horse who landed the most recent win in this field (1st, 5f, Good) and has David Nolan steering; Paul Midgley's yard is in fair form (1/16 over 14 days) and the 8-day turnaround suits a fit six-year-old who handles Good ground well at this trip.

runners_data.name: Betweenthesticks
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's six-year-old carries a visor and brings the best recent Good-ground profile in the field — two wins and six places from 11 similar-going runs — making James Sullivan's hold-up mount the most dangerous closing threat if the pace is strong enough to reel in Dream Deal.

runners_data.name: Storm Call
runners_data.note: Carries a visor and has a recent win over this trip on Good ground to recommend him; Billy Garritty partners Michael & David Easterby's four-year-old, whose trainer is in strong form (5/41 over 14 days), but his two Southwell turf runs in between that win and now may have blunted his edge slightly.

runners_data.name: Showtime Mahomes
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up performer on his form figures — all five recent runs at 6f on Southwell's Tapeta — who arrives for Grant Tuer after a 133-day break and is operating at a trip and surface combination he hasn't faced in recent races; mapped to midfield due to congestion of off-the-pace types, which is not his natural position.

runners_data.name: Dream Deal
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front runner here and the key pace-shape horse; Tim Easterby's seven-year-old won over this course and distance on Good ground recently, David Allan takes the ride, and with no rival to push the pace the controlled fractions he sets will define the entire race shape.

runners_data.name: Dandy Dinmont
runners_data.note: Nigel Tinkler's seven-year-old has a win over this trip on Good ground in recent form but also a run of double-figure finishes; though he races at the back naturally, the crowded hold-up sector means Rowan Scott will have to be creative to find clear daylight late on.

runners_data.name: Sea Her Excel
runners_data.note: Ivan Furtado's three-year-old has a strong profile on Good ground (5W/P from 7 similar-going runs) and a recent win over 6f; Elle-May Croot claims 5lb which is a useful weight allowance, but she's forced into a midfield map slot despite being a natural closer, and the shorter 5f trip is a minor query.

runners_data.name: Brave Empire
runners_data.note: Jason Hart partners this Furtado five-year-old who wears headgear (hood) but whose recent form figures — nine, eight, thirteen — on Good and Soft ground do not inspire confidence; no wins or places from five similar-going runs in the dataset, and the midfield mapping is not his natural position either.

runners_data.name: Cheerleader
runners_data.note: Tina Jackson's four-year-old has a win and two places from nine similar-ground runs, most recently finishing ninth after a 32-day break; Joanna Mason rides, but the horse's true hold-up style being compressed into midfield alongside half the field makes finding a clean passage difficult.

runners_data.name: Davorge Nation
runners_data.note: Listed as a non-runner — Declan Carroll's three-year-old has a win over 5f on Good ground and reasonable recent form, but with no jockey declared this runner must be treated as absent until confirmed otherwise; any late change could affect the pace map minimally given the surplus of hold-up types.

races.paceDynamic: Dream Deal is the sole confirmed front runner in this ten-horse field and, with no genuine rival to push the pace from the outset, should settle into a comfortable, uncontested lead over Pontefract's stiff five furlongs. The pace will be honest but controlled — Dream Deal has won off the front here at this trip in Good ground and David Allan will look to dictate from flag to finish without being harried. The bulk of the field are natural hold-up or off-the-pace types, meaning the race reduces to whether the chasers can close a gap that Dream Deal sets on his own terms. This shape heavily favours a prominent or early-to-lead profile, and the closers will need a strong gallop to reel in a horse allowed to lobster along unchallenged. The field holds considerably more hold-up horses than the map can accommodate at the rear — Showtime Mahomes, Sea Her Excel, Davorge Nation, Dandy Dinmont, Brave Empire and Cheerleader are all genuine off-the-pace types, and those most likely to actually secure a workable prominent position behind Dream Deal are the lightly-weighted, quicker-jumping hold-up horses with better recent Good-ground form such as Hover On The Wind, Betweenthesticks and Storm Call.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Dream Deal Dictates Alone
scenarios.trigger: If Dream Deal settles into an unchallenged lead and the closers are left with too much to do from their wide-field hold-up positions.
scenarios.body: Dream Deal controls fractions from flag to finish on a track where front runners with Good-ground form have a strong record over five furlongs; with no one able to challenge for the lead, the margin at the line could be greater than the market expects.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If Dream Deal sets a stronger gallop than expected, burning herself out and leaving the race open for the hold-up horses with the best Good-ground form to storm home.
scenarios.body: The pace collapses in the final furlong and the runners with the best finishing kicks — those who have most recently shown win form on Good ground over five furlongs — come through in a wall finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Fill Gaps
scenarios.trigger: If Dream Deal is tracked closely by one or two horses who push up from midfield sooner than expected, turning the race into a conventional pace-and-kick contest.
scenarios.body: A competitive early gallop plays to those sitting second or third, with superior class and recent form counting for more than raw finishing speed; horses with Good-ground wins at the trip and prominent records fill the frame.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Lands Blow
scenarios.trigger: If a redistributed hold-up horse races uncharacteristically handy and benefits from a tactical pace breakdown not anticipated in the pre-race shape.
scenarios.body: With so many horses compressed into midfield and running out of their natural role, a chaotic mid-race shuffle could produce a gap for a horse like Sea Her Excel or Dandy Dinmont to find a clear run when others are checked.

watchPoints.text: Dream Deal (David Allan) — monitor whether she gets a completely uncontested lead; if nothing tracks her within two lengths for the first furlong, she will set her own fractions and the race becomes hers to lose.

Betweenthesticks — watch the visor-wearing hold-up horse's position leaving the stalls; if James Sullivan is able to slot in third or fourth rather than deep hold-up, the horse's Good-ground win record makes her a serious danger to Dream Deal's lead.

Davorge Nation is listed as a non-runner — confirm declaration status before the off, as any late withdrawal changes nothing structurally but reduces the pack of hold-up horses competing for midfield slots.

Sea Her Excel and Dandy Dinmont — both redistributed true hold-up types forced into midfield; watch for traffic problems in the final two furlongs as multiple horses with the same instinct to come from off the pace converge in a narrow corridor.

Storm Call (visor) — check the market move nearer post time; the Easterby yard's strong 14-day strike rate (5/41) and the horse's Good-ground win at this trip mean any market support should be respected despite the recent Southwell runs.
